name: aggregate-too-large
summary: An aggregate with more entities than its product's max_entities_per_aggregate setting.
explanation: The setting is the product's product_setting row (7 when it has none). An aggregate is the smallest cluster of entities that must stay consistent after one command: one transaction changes it, and everything in it is loaded, locked and saved together. Most need a root and a few children; one that holds many entities is usually several clusters that change at different times, held together only by references, so every command pays for all of them and two people's changes clash for no reason. A rule that spans two aggregates is checked by a specification, or followed through an event and a policy. Split it into smaller aggregates that each change together.
query:
WITH sized AS (
  SELECT aggregate_id, count(*) AS n FROM entity GROUP BY aggregate_id
)
SELECT a.id AS record,
       'Aggregate ' || a.id || ' has ' || z.n || ' entities, more than the ' || coalesce(ps.max_entities_per_aggregate, 7)
       || ' that the product''s max_entities_per_aggregate setting allows; split it into smaller aggregates that each change together.' AS message
FROM aggregate a
JOIN sized z ON z.aggregate_id = a.id
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = a.id
LEFT JOIN product_setting ps ON ps.product_id = s.product_id
WHERE z.n > coalesce(ps.max_entities_per_aggregate, 7)
ORDER BY record

name: domain-named-for-technology
summary: A domain is named for a technology layer or delivery channel rather than a business capability.
explanation: A domain is a vertical slice of business capability: it owns its model, its use cases, their interaction design, the technical records that implement them and their tests. Technology is expressed through the technical kinds inside each domain, never as a domain of its own. A domain whose title or domain code (its ID after the product prefix, such as LEND in TL-LEND) names a technology splits one capability across several domains. The words are web app, frontend, front end, backend, back end, API, UI, server, database, DB, desktop, mobile, engine, infrastructure, infra and Electron, matched as whole words in any letter case, with or without a space or hyphen inside the two-word ones, and in the plural. Only the title and code are read, never the description. Name the domain for the capability it serves.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Domain ' || id || ' is named for a technology, not a business capability: '
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' THEN 'its title "' || trim(title) || '" says "' || in_title || '"' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_title <> '' AND in_code <> '' THEN ' and ' ELSE '' END
       || CASE WHEN in_code <> '' THEN 'its code ' || code || ' says "' || in_code || '"' ELSE '' END
       || '; name the domain for the capability it serves, and make the technology a layer in each domain''s Design stage.' AS message
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, code,
         regexp_extract(lower(title), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_title,
         regexp_extract(lower(code), '(^|[^a-z])(' || words || ')([^a-z]|$)', 2) AS in_code
  FROM (
    SELECT id, title, CASE WHEN starts_with(id, product_id || '-') THEN substr(id, length(product_id) + 2) ELSE id END AS code
    FROM domain
  ),
  (SELECT 'web[ -]?apps?|front[ -]?ends?|back[ -]?ends?|apis?|uis?|servers?|databases?|dbs?|desktops?|mobile'
          || '|engines?|infrastructure|infra|electron' AS words)
)
WHERE in_title <> '' OR in_code <> ''
ORDER BY record

name: endpoint-route-not-in-file
summary: An endpoint whose handler's file does not name its method and route.
explanation: An endpoint handler serves its endpoint's method and route, so its file names both: the route, written any way routes are written (`/tools/{toolId}`, `/tools/:toolId`, `/tools/<tool-id>`, `/tools/[toolId]`, a template's `${toolId}`, or a regular expression literal that matches it, such as `/^\/tools\/(\d+)$/`), in code, a string or a comment. Parameters match whatever their names, and only the path counts: a query string or fragment is not part of a route. The method is written in capitals, or called as `.post(`, on the route's line or within two lines of it. Then a reader of the record finds the code, and a route changed on one side and not the other is caught. A handler whose file does not exist yet is technical-file-missing instead. Correct the endpoint's method or route, or point its handler at the file that serves it.
query:
SELECT r.record,
       'Endpoint ' || r.record || ' is ' || r.method || ' ' || r.route || ', but its handler''s file ' || r.files
       || ' does not name that route with that method; correct the endpoint, or point its handler at the file that serves it.' AS message
FROM route_facts r
WHERE r.kind = 'endpoint' AND r.files <> '' AND NOT r.found
ORDER BY record

name: entity-unreferenced
summary: A child entity that its aggregate's root does not reach.
explanation: Each child entity is a part of its aggregate's root, so a `has_one` or `has_many` reaches it from the root, directly or through other children of the same aggregate. Links that cross aggregates (has-crosses-aggregate) do not count. Link the child from the root or from another child with `has_one` or `has_many`.
query:
WITH RECURSIVE
  roots AS (SELECT aggregate_id, id AS root FROM entity WHERE role = 'root'),
  parts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.source_id AS source, l.target_id AS target
    FROM (SELECT source_id, target_id FROM has_one UNION ALL SELECT source_id, target_id FROM has_many) l
    JOIN entity s ON s.id = l.source_id
    JOIN entity t ON t.id = l.target_id AND t.aggregate_id = s.aggregate_id
  ),
  reached (id) AS (
    SELECT root FROM roots
    UNION
    SELECT p.target FROM parts p JOIN reached r ON r.id = p.source
  )
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Child entity ' || e.id || ' is not reached from ' || e.aggregate_id || '''s root ' || r.root
       || ' by has_one or has_many; link it from ' || r.root || ' or from the child it is a part of.' AS message
FROM entity e
JOIN roots r ON r.aggregate_id = e.aggregate_id
WHERE e.role = 'child' AND e.id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM reached)
ORDER BY record

name: event-not-by-outbox
summary: An event a policy hears, whose aggregate is stored in a database table, whose event type is not delivered by outbox.
explanation: An event a policy hears is delivered by outbox: saved in the same transaction as its aggregate and delivered reliably afterwards, since a lost reaction is a lost change. That is every event a policy hears whose aggregate is stored in a database table (an entity of the aggregate has a table whose storage is `table`), in its own domain or, when published, in another. An event inside one process with no transaction to join, such as one whose aggregate is kept in browser storage, a file or in memory and is heard in the same browser tab or process, is exempt. So is an event that only keeps read models current (fed_by), where those read models are rebuilt from the data on every load: it may be delivered in process, since the next load rebuilds what a lost delivery missed. Its event type records the delivery; one a policy hears that is delivered in process, with no delivery given, or no event type at all, leaves the reaction to chance. Give the event an event type delivered by outbox.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Domain event ' || e.id || ' is heard by policy ' || (SELECT string_agg(h.source_id, ', ' ORDER BY h.source_id) FROM hears h WHERE h.target_id = e.id)
       || CASE WHEN t.id IS NULL THEN ', but has no event type; give it one delivered by outbox.'
               WHEN t.delivery IS NULL THEN ', but its event type ' || t.id || ' gives no delivery; deliver it by outbox.'
               ELSE ', but its event type ' || t.id || ' is delivered ' || t.delivery || '; deliver it by outbox.' END AS message
FROM domain_event e
LEFT JOIN event_type t ON t.domain_event_id = e.id
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hears h WHERE h.target_id = e.id)
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "table" tb JOIN entity en ON en.id = tb.entity_id WHERE en.aggregate_id = e.aggregate_id AND tb.storage = 'table')
  AND (t.delivery IS NULL OR t.delivery <> 'outbox')
ORDER BY record

name: event-tense
summary: A domain event's title reads as something that happened, in the past tense.
explanation: An event is named for what happened, such as Loan opened or Payment sent. The check is a heuristic over the title's words, in any letter case and split at anything but a letter: the title passes when its last word, or any word after its first (the word after a one-word subject, as in Loan became overdue), is a past form. A past form is a word of four or more letters ending in "-ed", other than the few such words that are not verbs in the past (need, seed, feed, speed, breed, bleed, embed, proceed, exceed, succeed, hundred, naked, sacred, wicked), or one of the irregular past forms the query lists. The heuristic can miss a past form it does not know, so this is a warning. Name the event in the past tense, as what happened (Tool returned, not Return tool), or add the word to the check's list if it is a past form the check does not know.
query:
SELECT e.id AS record,
       'Event ' || e.id || ' is titled "' || trim(e.title)
       || '", which does not read as past tense; name it for what happened, such as "Loan opened" or "Tool returned".' AS message
FROM domain_event e
WHERE regexp_matches(lower(e.title), '[a-z]')
  AND e.id NOT IN (
    SELECT w.id
    FROM (
      SELECT id, unnest(words) AS word, unnest(generate_series(1, len(words))) AS position, len(words) AS count
      FROM (SELECT id, string_split(trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z]+', ' ', 'g')), ' ') AS words FROM domain_event)
    ) w
    WHERE (w.position > 1 OR w.position = w.count)
      AND (list_contains(string_split(
      'arose arisen ate eaten awoke awoken became begun began bent bound bit bitten blew blown broke broken bred '
      || 'brought built burnt bought caught chose chosen came cost crept cut dealt dug did done drew drawn dreamt '
      || 'drank drunk drove driven fell fallen fed felt fought found fled flew flown forbade forbidden forgot '
      || 'forgotten forgave forgiven froze frozen got gotten gave given went gone grew grown hung had heard hid '
      || 'hidden hit held hurt kept knew known laid led leant learnt left lent let lit lost made meant met mistook '
      || 'mistaken overdone overran overridden overrode overtaken overtook paid put quit read rebuilt redone remade '
      || 'reran rerun reset resent resold retook retaken rewound rewrote rewritten rode ridden rang rung rose risen '
      || 'ran run said saw seen sought sold sent set shook shaken shone shot showed shown shut sang sung sank sunk '
      || 'sat slept slid spoke spoken sped spent spun split spread sprang sprung stood stole stolen stuck struck '
      || 'swore sworn swept swam swum swung took taken taught tore torn told thought threw thrown understood undid '
      || 'undone upheld upset withdrew withdrawn withheld woke woken wore worn won wound wrote written', ' '), w.word)
           OR (length(w.word) >= 4 AND w.word LIKE '%ed' AND NOT list_contains(string_split(
      'need seed feed speed breed bleed embed proceed exceed succeed hundred naked sacred wicked', ' '), w.word)))
  )
ORDER BY record

name: flow-test-level-for-interface
summary: A flow test at a level that does not fit its flow's interface.
explanation: A flow test walks its flow's main path the way its interface is used: in a real browser or the desktop shell (browser) for a web app or a desktop app, and from outside the running product through its requests or commands (system) for an API, a CLI or agent tools. A manual test names the level the person exercises, so it is held to the same fit. A flow through an interface of kind other may be tested at any level a flow test allows. Run the test at the level that fits, or give the flow the interface it really goes through.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       'Flow test ' || t.id || ' runs at level ' || t.level || ', but its flow ' || f.id || ' goes through ' || i.id || ', an interface of kind ' || i.kind
       || ', which is tested at ' || CASE WHEN i.kind IN ('web app', 'desktop') THEN 'browser' ELSE 'system' END || '.' AS message
FROM flow_test t
JOIN flow f ON f.id = t.flow_id
JOIN interface i ON i.id = f.interface_id
WHERE (i.kind IN ('web app', 'desktop') AND t.level <> 'browser') OR (i.kind IN ('API', 'CLI', 'agent tools') AND t.level <> 'system')
ORDER BY record

name: flow-title-off-pattern
summary: A flow whose title is not its use case's title, then in or through, then its interface's title.
explanation: A use case has one flow per interface it happens through, so a flow's title is its use case's title with its interface's: "Borrow a tool in the web app", "Borrow a tool through the HTTP API". Then each flow of a use case reads as the same goal in another place, and a renamed use case or interface shows in every flow that still has the old title. The check compares in any letter case and allows "in" or "through", with or without "the" before the interface. Retitle the flow as its use case's title, then in or through, then its interface's title.
query:
SELECT f.id AS record,
       'Flow ' || f.id || ' is titled "' || trim(f.title) || '", but its use case ' || u.id || ' is "' || trim(u.title) || '" and its interface ' || i.id || ' is "' || trim(i.title) || '"; title it "' || trim(u.title) || CASE WHEN i.kind IN ('web app', 'desktop') THEN ' in the ' ELSE ' through the ' END || CASE WHEN regexp_matches(trim(i.title), '^[A-Z][a-z]') THEN lower(left(trim(i.title), 1)) || substr(trim(i.title), 2) ELSE trim(i.title) END || '".' AS message
FROM flow f
JOIN use_case u ON u.id = f.use_case_id
JOIN interface i ON i.id = f.interface_id
WHERE NOT list_contains(
  [lower(trim(u.title)) || ' in ' || lower(trim(i.title)), lower(trim(u.title)) || ' in the ' || lower(trim(i.title)),
   lower(trim(u.title)) || ' through ' || lower(trim(i.title)), lower(trim(u.title)) || ' through the ' || lower(trim(i.title))],
  lower(trim(f.title)))
ORDER BY record

name: has-crosses-aggregate
summary: A `has_one` or `has_many` link stays inside its aggregate.
explanation: These relations link an entity to its parts, and parts belong to their aggregate, so both ends sit in the same aggregate. Aggregates refer to each other by ID only: a field typed by the other aggregate. Type a field by the other aggregate instead, or move the part into the aggregate.
query:
SELECT l.source_id AS record,
       'Entity ' || l.source_id || ' ' || l.relation || ' ' || l.target_id || ', which sits in ' || t.aggregate_id
       || ', not in ' || s.aggregate_id || '; a part belongs to its aggregate, so refer to ' || t.aggregate_id
       || ' by a field typed by it, or move ' || l.target_id || ' into ' || s.aggregate_id || '.' AS message
FROM (SELECT 'has_one' AS relation, source_id, target_id FROM has_one
      UNION ALL SELECT 'has_many', source_id, target_id FROM has_many) l
JOIN entity s ON s.id = l.source_id
JOIN entity t ON t.id = l.target_id
WHERE s.aggregate_id <> t.aggregate_id
ORDER BY record, message

name: integration-unused
summary: A integration that nothing uses.
explanation: A integration has no owner: it exists because flow steps exchange with it. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the steps that exchange with it with exchanges_with, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Integration ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: flow steps exchange with it; link the steps that exchange with it with exchanges_with, or remove it.' AS message
FROM integration r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM exchanges_with x WHERE x.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: lone-child
summary: A capability or a group with exactly one child.
explanation: A level that holds one record groups nothing. A capability with exactly one child is reported, counting its own children of every kind (its use cases, and the records of a product's own kinds under it) but not theirs; one with none is a coverage gap instead. A group (the `group_name` of every kind that has one, read from the record_group view: terms, UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and a product's own kinds) is counted among its parent's children of one kind, compared trimmed and in any letter case, and reported on that parent. Merge it into a neighbor, or give it more.
query:
SELECT r.parent_id AS record,
       'Capability ' || r.parent_id || ' has only one ' || lower(any_value(k.label)) || ', ' || any_value(r.id) || '; merge it into a neighboring capability, or give it more.' AS message
FROM record_parent r JOIN capability c ON c.id = r.parent_id JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = r.kind
GROUP BY r.parent_id
HAVING count(*) = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT m.parent, pk.label || ' ' || m.parent || '''s group "' || m.label
       || '" has only one ' || lower(k.label) || ', ' || m.child || '; merge it into a neighboring group, or give it more.'
FROM (
  SELECT r.parent_id AS parent, r.kind, lower(trim(g.label)) AS bucket, min(trim(g.label)) AS label, count(*) AS n, any_value(r.id) AS child
  FROM record_group g JOIN record_parent r ON r.id = g.id
  WHERE r.kind <> 'flow_step'
  GROUP BY r.parent_id, r.kind, lower(trim(g.label))
) m
JOIN record_id p ON p.id = m.parent
JOIN meta_kind pk ON pk.name = p.kind
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = m.kind
WHERE m.n = 1
ORDER BY record, message

name: manual-test-file-silent
summary: A manual test whose file exists but never mentions it.
explanation: A manual test may name a file that holds the steps a person follows. Nothing ties that file to the test until it names the test's ID. Manual tests are not held to the automated rule (test-file-missing-id), so a silent file is a warning. Name the test in the file, or point its `file` at the file that carries it out.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' names the file ' || t.file || ', but that file does not mention ' || t.id
       || '; name the test in the file, or point its file at the one that carries it out.' AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = t.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE t.state = 'manual' AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id
ORDER BY record

name: not-built
summary: An obligation not every file of what implements it exists for yet, as coverage counts it.
explanation: Coverage counts an obligation as built once every technical record that implements it names a file that exists, and there is at least one: a constraint's value type, an invariant's data model (any one of its aggregate's) or the table whose unique key names it, a specification's predicate, a policy's event handler, a domain service's service, a UC requirement's command or query handlers with the predicates and services of what they check or call, or the UI components of the views its steps happen in, a view requirement's UI components, an API requirement's endpoint handler, a standard rule's meeting records. A pattern rule asks for proof only. This warning names exactly the obligations coverage lists as not built. Add the technical record with its file, or write each file it names.
query: SELECT id AS record, message FROM coverage_gap WHERE missing = 'built' ORDER BY record, domain NULLS LAST

name: not-designed
summary: An obligation whose implementation is not specified yet, as coverage counts it.
explanation: Coverage counts an obligation as designed once its implementation is specified: a UC requirement once a step of its use case's flow fulfills it, a standard rule once a technical record meets it, a product's own obligation once a record links to it with a design relation. A constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, view requirement and API requirement are designed by construction, and a pattern rule wherever it is owed. This warning names exactly the obligations coverage lists as not designed, so the two never disagree. Fulfill the UC requirement from a step of its flow, or link what designs the obligation.
query: SELECT id AS record, message FROM coverage_gap WHERE missing = 'designed' ORDER BY record, domain NULLS LAST

name: not-proved
summary: An obligation no automated or manual test at an allowed level proves yet, as coverage counts it.
explanation: Coverage counts an obligation as proved once a test of it is automated or manual, at a level its test kind allows, and, when automated, its file exists and names the test's ID. A pattern rule is reported once for each domain that owes it, proved there only by its pattern rule test naming that domain. A test not automated yet does not prove, and the message says so. This warning names exactly the obligations coverage lists as not proved. Write the test, automate it or run it by hand, at a level its kind allows.
query: SELECT id AS record, message FROM coverage_gap WHERE missing = 'proved' ORDER BY record, domain NULLS LAST

name: package-not-in-manifest
summary: A record names a package that none of its product's package.json files lists.
explanation: A package_use row says a technical record uses a package, so that every dependency is accounted for by what it serves. Naming a package no manifest lists is a stale or mistyped claim: the package was removed, renamed or never added, and the record no longer tells the truth about the code. Fix the name, add the dependency to the package.json the code runs from, or remove the package_use row.
query:
SELECT u.record_id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || u.record_id || ' names package ' || u.package || ', which no package.json of its product lists.' AS message
FROM package_use u
JOIN record_id r ON r.id = u.record_id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = r.kind
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM package_facts f WHERE f.package = u.package)
ORDER BY record, u.package

name: pattern-not-followed
summary: A pattern that no use case and no domain follows.
explanation: No domain owes its rules, so they count in no domain's coverage. Link the use cases or domains that follow it with `follows`, or remove the pattern if nothing needs it.
query:
SELECT p.id AS record,
       'No use case or domain follows pattern ' || p.id || ', so '
       || CASE p.rules WHEN 0 THEN 'it is not used anywhere.'
                       WHEN 1 THEN 'its 1 rule is not counted in any domain''s coverage.'
                       ELSE 'its ' || p.rules || ' rules are not counted in any domain''s coverage.' END AS message
FROM (SELECT p.id, (SELECT count(*) FROM pattern_rule r WHERE r.pattern_id = p.id) AS rules FROM pattern p) p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM follows f WHERE f.target_id = p.id)
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-rule-test-outside-followers
summary: A pattern rule test names a domain that follows its pattern and owes its rule.
explanation: A pattern rule test proves its rule in one domain that follows the pattern: the domain itself follows it, or one of its use cases does. A test naming a domain that does not follow the pattern proves the rule where nothing owes it, an error. One naming a following domain where the rule is waived (every following use case there marks its setting not applicable, or no follower there meets its applies-when setting) counts for nothing, a warning. Name a domain that owes the rule, link the domain or its use case to the pattern with `follows`, or remove the test.
query:
SELECT CASE WHEN NOT f.follows THEN 'error' ELSE 'warning' END AS severity, t.id AS record,
       'Pattern rule test ' || t.id || ' proves rule ' || t.pattern_rule_id || ' in domain ' || t.domain_id || ', '
       || CASE WHEN NOT f.follows THEN 'which does not follow pattern ' || r.pattern_id || '; name a domain that does, or link ' || t.domain_id || ' or one of its use cases to the pattern with follows.'
               ELSE 'where the rule is not applicable or waived, so the test counts for nothing; name a domain that owes the rule, or remove the test.' END AS message
FROM pattern_rule_test t
JOIN pattern_rule r ON r.id = t.pattern_rule_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM follows x JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = x.source_id
  WHERE x.target_id = r.pattern_id AND s.domain_id = t.domain_id) AS follows) f
WHERE NOT f.follows OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM owed_pattern_rules o WHERE o.id = t.pattern_rule_id AND o.domain = t.domain_id)
ORDER BY record

name: pattern-setting-missing
summary: A use case that follows a pattern gives each of the pattern's settings.
explanation: Each setting of the pattern (a pattern_setting row) needs a setting_value row from each use case that follows it: a value, or a reason it is not applicable. A domain that follows a pattern itself owes every rule and gives no settings. Give the missing setting a value, or say why it is not applicable.
query:
SELECT f.source_id AS record,
       'Use case ' || f.source_id || ' follows pattern ' || f.target_id || ' but gives no value for its setting "' || s.name
       || '"; give it a value, or say why it is not applicable.' AS message
FROM follows f
JOIN use_case u ON u.id = f.source_id
JOIN pattern_setting s ON s.pattern_id = f.target_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM setting_value v WHERE v.follower_id = f.source_id AND v.pattern_id = f.target_id AND v.setting = s.name)
ORDER BY record, message

name: query-title-verb
summary: A query whose title does not start with Get, List or Find.
explanation: A query asks for data and changes nothing, so its title starts with the verb that says what comes back: Get for one thing, List for several, Find for a search, such as "Get a member's loans", "List overdue loans" or "Find a tool by name". A query titled like a command ("Check the workspace", "Export a theme") reads as a change. Retitle the query with Get, List or Find.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Query ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which does not start with Get, List or Find; title a query by what it returns, such as "List overdue loans".' AS message
FROM query
WHERE NOT regexp_matches(trim(title), '^(get|list|find)([^a-z]|$)', 'i')
ORDER BY record

name: repository-persists-nothing
summary: A repository that persists no aggregate.
explanation: A repository exists to load and save its aggregate, whole, and says which with its one persists link; other aggregates it also persists are recorded exceptions (repository_share rows). One that persists none is a leftover, or its link is missing. Link the aggregate it persists with persists, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Repository ' || r.id || ' persists no aggregate: link the aggregate it loads and saves with persists, or remove it.' AS message
FROM repository r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM persists p WHERE p.source_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: specification-title-article
summary: A specification whose title starts with an article: A, An or The.
explanation: A specification is a yes/no condition a record meets or not, and its title names that condition with no article, such as "Tool is available" or "Member in good standing", so a command's or query's list of the specifications it checks reads as a list of conditions. Drop the article from the start of the title.
query:
SELECT id AS record,
       'Specification ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which starts with "' || regexp_extract(trim(title), '^[A-Za-z]+') || '"; name the condition with no article, such as "Tool is available".' AS message
FROM specification
WHERE regexp_matches(trim(title), '^(a|an|the)\s', 'i')
ORDER BY record

name: specification-unused
summary: A specification that nothing uses.
explanation: A specification has no owner: it exists because commands check it and queries select by it. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the commands that check it or the queries that select by it, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Specification ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: commands check it and queries select by it; link the commands that check it or the queries that select by it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM specification r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM checks c WHERE c.target_id = r.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM selects_by q WHERE q.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: step-order
summary: The steps on each path of a flow are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, without gaps.
explanation: A flow's steps are read in `position` within their `path`, a short name such as main or refused, compared trimmed and in any letter case. The schema gives each step a whole number that no other step on its path has; a path whose positions skip a number is reported once, on the first step after the gap. Renumber the steps of the path to close the gap.
query:
WITH steps AS (
  SELECT id, flow_id AS parent, lower(trim(path)) AS step_path, position AS n FROM flow_step
),
paths AS (
  SELECT parent, step_path, max(n) AS top FROM steps GROUP BY parent, step_path
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT p.parent, p.step_path, min(m) AS first_missing, string_agg(m::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY m) AS missing_list
  FROM paths p CROSS JOIN range(1, p.top) t(m)
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = p.parent AND x.step_path = p.step_path AND x.n = t.m)
  GROUP BY p.parent, p.step_path
)
SELECT s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ' has position ' || s.n
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' on path ' || s.step_path END
       || ' in flow ' || s.parent || ', but no step'
       || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN '' ELSE ' of that path' END || ' has position ' || g.missing_list
       || '; number the steps of ' || CASE WHEN s.step_path = 'main' THEN 'a flow' ELSE 'a path' END
       || ' 1, 2, 3 and so on, with no gaps.' AS message
FROM gaps g
JOIN steps s ON s.parent = g.parent AND s.step_path = g.step_path
WHERE s.n = (SELECT min(x.n) FROM steps x WHERE x.parent = g.parent AND x.step_path = g.step_path AND x.n > g.first_missing)
ORDER BY record, message

name: step-without-endpoint
summary: A step of a flow through an API that invokes a command or query no endpoint exposes.
explanation: A flow through an interface of kind API happens as requests: each step that invokes a command or query calls the endpoint that exposes it, so an endpoint must expose what the step invokes. (A step of a flow through a web app, a desktop app, a CLI or agent tools names its command or query the same way; only an API's are reached through endpoints. A step of an API, CLI or agent tools flow that happens in a view is refused by the store, step-fits-interface.) Add the endpoint under the command or query, or have the step invoke what an endpoint exposes.
query:
SELECT s.id AS record,
       'Flow step ' || s.id || ' goes through ' || i.id || ', an API, so it calls an endpoint, but no endpoint exposes ' || v.target_id
       || ', which it invokes; add one under ' || v.target_id || ', or have the step invoke what an endpoint exposes.' AS message
FROM flow_step s
JOIN flow f ON f.id = s.flow_id
JOIN interface i ON i.id = f.interface_id AND i.kind = 'API'
JOIN invokes v ON v.source_id = s.id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM endpoint e WHERE e.command_id = v.target_id OR e.query_id = v.target_id)
ORDER BY record

name: table-schema-mismatch
summary: A table kept in a database whose file does not define it as the spec says: its name, a column or a key.
explanation: A table, view or materialized view that names a file is checked against that file read as text (a migration, a SQL schema, or code that creates it): the file defines a table or view of its name; every column its entity's or read model's fields give (a field's column_name, else its name in lower case with underscores; a value object of several fields flattened into its fields' columns; an entity's table also holds the fields of the children kept in its root's table); and each primary, unique and foreign key by its columns, a foreign key also by its target table. It recognizes CREATE TABLE and CREATE VIEW (OR REPLACE, TEMP, MATERIALIZED, IF NOT EXISTS) with their column definitions and inline or table PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE and REFERENCES, the columns an AS SELECT body selects or names with AS, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX and ALTER TABLE ... ADD. It does not compare types, NOT NULL, CHECKs, a unique key's name or condition, or index keys, and it cannot see a statement built at run time from pieces the text does not show. A missing file is technical-file-missing instead. Change the file to match, or the spec when the file is right.
query:
SELECT f.record,
       'Table ' || f.record || ' names ' || f.file || ', which '
       || CASE f.part
            WHEN 'table' THEN 'defines no table or view named ' || f.expected
            WHEN 'column' THEN 'gives ' || f.name || ' no column ' || f.expected
            ELSE 'gives ' || f.name || ' no ' || f.part || ' key ' || f.expected
          END || '.' AS message
FROM table_facts f
WHERE NOT f.found
ORDER BY f.record, CASE f.part WHEN 'table' THEN 1 WHEN 'column' THEN 2 WHEN 'primary' THEN 3 WHEN 'unique' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END, f.expected

name: technical-file-missing
summary: A technical record whose file does not exist yet.
explanation: The technical specification may name a file before it is written, so this is work to do, not breakage: until the file exists, what the record implements is not built. A technical record's file may be a file or a folder of files under the product root. Write the file, or fix the path (relative to the product root).
query:
SELECT f.record,
       k.label || ' ' || f.record || ' names ' || f.file || ', which does not exist yet.' AS message
FROM file_facts f
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE NOT f.file_exists AND f.kind NOT IN (SELECT kind FROM test_level_allowed) AND f.kind <> 'test_data_set'
ORDER BY record

name: term-used-unlinked
summary: A term's meaning uses another term of its product by title without a builds_on link to it.
explanation: Definitions build up, never in a circle (LA-STD-MODELING-R12): a term is defined only by plain words and terms below it, and names each one it uses with builds_on, so the store can refuse a loop. The check reads each meaning in lower case, with text in backticks left out as code, and looks for every other term of the product by title as a whole word, singular or plural (a title ending in a consonant and y also as -ies); a shorter title found only inside a longer term's title (Domain inside Domain event) does not count. It cannot tell a word used in another sense, so it is a warning. Link the term with builds_on to the term it uses, or say it in plain words.
query:
WITH term_in AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.title, s.product_id,
         lower(regexp_replace(t.meaning, '`[^`]*`', ' ', 'g')) AS meaning,
         CASE WHEN regexp_matches(lower(trim(t.title)), '[^aeiou]y$')
              THEN regexp_replace(left(lower(trim(t.title)), -1), '([.*+?^$(){}|\[\]\\])', '\\\1', 'g') || '(y|ies)'
              ELSE regexp_replace(lower(trim(t.title)), '([.*+?^$(){}|\[\]\\])', '\\\1', 'g') || '(s|es)?' END AS word
  FROM term t
  JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = t.id
),
longer AS (
  SELECT b.id, string_agg(c.word, '|') AS words
  FROM term_in b
  JOIN term_in c ON c.product_id = b.product_id AND c.id <> b.id AND length(c.title) > length(b.title)
   AND regexp_matches(lower(c.title), '(^|[^a-z0-9])' || b.word || '($|[^a-z0-9])')
  GROUP BY b.id
)
SELECT a.id AS record,
       'Term ' || a.id || ' (' || a.title || ') uses "' || b.title || '" in its meaning but does not build on ' || b.id
       || ': link it with builds_on, or say it in plain words.' AS message
FROM term_in a
JOIN term_in b ON b.product_id = a.product_id AND b.id <> a.id
LEFT JOIN longer l ON l.id = b.id
WHERE regexp_matches(
        CASE WHEN l.words IS NULL THEN a.meaning
             ELSE regexp_replace(a.meaning, '(^|[^a-z0-9])(' || l.words || ')($|[^a-z0-9])', '\1 \3', 'g') END,
        '(^|[^a-z0-9])' || b.word || '($|[^a-z0-9])')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM builds_on k WHERE k.source_id = a.id AND k.target_id = b.id)
ORDER BY record, b.id

name: test-case-unnamed
summary: A test case in the product's test files names a test whose file it is in, so every test in the code leads back to the record it proves.
explanation: test-file-missing-id follows a test record to its code; this check follows the code back. The engine reads the product's test files (those matching the tests globs in lathe.config.json, by default **/*.test.{ts,tsx,js,mjs} and **/*.spec.{ts,tsx,js}, never in node_modules, dist or another product's folder, and every file a test record names) as text and finds each test case: a call of it or test, with its modifiers and each forms, whose name is a string or template literal, inside the describe calls around it. A test case must name, in its own name, its describes' names or its each rows, the ID of a test (or of a product kind's record that proves an obligation) whose file is the file it is in. One that names none proves nothing anyone can find. Start its name, or its describe's, with the ID of the test it proves, adding that test when the spec lacks it, or remove the test case if it proves nothing.
query:
SELECT NULL AS record,
       c.file || ':' || c.line || ': the test case "' || c.name || '" names no test whose file is ' || c.file
       || '; start its name, or its describe''s, with the ID of the test it proves, or remove it if it proves nothing.' AS message
FROM test_case c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM test_case_id i JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = i.id
  WHERE i.file = c.file AND i.position = c.position AND f.path = c.file
    AND (f.kind IN (SELECT kind FROM test_level_allowed)
      -- A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation stands in for a test.
      OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = f.record)))
ORDER BY c.file, c.position

name: test-data-set-file-missing
summary: A test data set whose file does not exist.
explanation: A test data set's file is the seed or fixture that builds it, a file or a folder of files under the product root. When an automated test starts from it, a missing file means that test cannot run, so it is an error. Otherwise the plan may name the file before it is written, so it is a warning. Write the file, or fix the path (relative to the product root).
query:
SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM starts_from s JOIN test_run t ON t.id = s.source_id WHERE s.target_id = f.record AND t.state = 'automated') THEN 'error' ELSE 'warning' END AS severity,
       f.record,
       'Test data set ' || f.record || ' names ' || f.file || ', which does not exist'
       || CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM starts_from s JOIN test_run t ON t.id = s.source_id WHERE s.target_id = f.record AND t.state = 'automated') THEN ', so the automated tests that start from it cannot run.' ELSE ' yet.' END AS message
FROM file_facts f
WHERE f.kind = 'test_data_set' AND NOT f.file_exists
ORDER BY record

name: test-data-set-unused
summary: A test data set that no test starts from.
explanation: A test data set exists because tests start from it: it is prepared before them and reset after. One that no test starts from is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the tests that start from it with starts_from, or remove it.
query:
SELECT d.id AS record, 'Test data set ' || d.id || ' is used by nothing: tests start from it; link the tests that start from it with starts_from, or remove it.' AS message
FROM test_data_set d
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM starts_from s WHERE s.target_id = d.id)
ORDER BY record

name: test-file-missing
summary: A test's `file` exists, and so does that of a product kind's record that proves an obligation.
explanation: For an automated or manual test a missing file is an error. A test that is not automated yet may name the file it will live in, so for it a missing file is a warning. The file must be a file under the product root, never a folder. A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation and names a file is checked as an automated test is. Fix the path (relative to the product root), or write the file.
query:
SELECT CASE WHEN t.state = 'not automated yet' THEN 'warning' ELSE 'error' END AS severity, t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' names the file ' || t.file || ', which does not exist'
       || CASE WHEN t.state = 'not automated yet' THEN ' yet.' ELSE '.' END AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = t.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE NOT f.file_exists
UNION ALL
-- A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation stands in for a test, and its file is checked as one.
SELECT 'error', f.record, k.label || ' ' || f.record || ' names the file ' || f.file || ', which does not exist.'
FROM file_facts f JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE k.product_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = f.record) AND NOT f.file_exists
ORDER BY record

name: test-file-missing-id
summary: An automated test's file names the test, and so does that of a product kind's record that proves an obligation, so the code can be traced back to it.
explanation: A test proves exactly its parent, and its file names the test's own ID as a whole ID (TL-LEND-INV01-T, not inside TL-LEND-INV01-T2), so a reader of the code finds the record and a reader of the record finds the code. Until it does, the test proves nothing. A missing file is test-file-missing instead; manual tests and tests not automated yet are not checked here. A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation and names a file is held to the same rule, since it counts as proof only when its file names it. Put the test's ID in the test's name in the file.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' names the file ' || t.file || ', but that file does not mention ' || t.id
       || '; put the ID in the test''s name in the file.' AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN file_facts f ON f.record = t.id
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE t.state = 'automated' AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id
UNION ALL
-- A record of a product's own kind that proves an obligation stands in for a test, and its file must name it as one's must.
SELECT f.record,
       k.label || ' ' || f.record || ' names the file ' || f.file || ', but that file does not mention ' || f.record
       || '; put the ID in the test''s name in the file.'
FROM file_facts f JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = f.kind
WHERE k.product_id IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM link l JOIN meta_relation r ON r.name = l.relation AND r.role = 'proof' WHERE l.source_id = f.record) AND f.file_exists AND NOT f.contains_id
ORDER BY record

name: test-level-not-allowed
summary: A test whose run by level its test kind does not allow.
explanation: A test's level says only how it runs, cheapest first: unit (in process, no storage or I/O), integration (in process, with real storage: a database, files, git), service (through the product's interface in process, with real storage), system (the running product driven from outside through its real interface) and browser (a real browser or the desktop shell against the running app); a manual test names the level a person exercises. Each test kind is run at the levels that can prove what it tests, and a test runs at the lowest of them that can observe its result: a constraint test at unit or integration (a constraint enforced by a SQL CHECK can only be tested against the database); an invariant or specification test at unit or integration; a domain service test at unit; a policy test at integration, service or system, or at browser where only the running app shows the reaction; a use case test at service, system or browser; a view test at unit or browser; an endpoint test at service or system; a flow test at system or browser (and at the one that fits its flow's interface, flow-test-level-for-interface); an integration test at integration, service or system; a pattern rule or standard rule test at any level. A test at another level proves nothing in coverage. Run the test at an allowed level and set its level, or make it the test kind of what it really proves.
query:
SELECT t.id AS record,
       k.label || ' ' || t.id || ' runs at level ' || t.level || ', which a ' || lower(k.label) || ' does not allow; run it at '
       || (SELECT string_agg(a.level::VARCHAR, ', ' ORDER BY a.level) FROM test_level_allowed a WHERE a.kind = t.kind) || '.' AS message
FROM test_run t
JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = t.kind
WHERE NOT t.level_allowed
ORDER BY record

name: test-title-not-a-result
summary: A test titled by what it does or ought to do, starting with "Tests that" or "Should", rather than by the result it shows.
explanation: A test's title is the observable result it shows, one short sentence that is true when the test passes, such as "An overdue loan is refused a renewal": a reader of the test plan learns what holds without opening the test. A title that starts with "Tests that", "Test that", "Tests whether", "Tests if" or "Should" says what the test checks or hopes for instead. A title that only starts with the noun "Tests", such as "Tests run in order", is not read. Rewrite the title as the result.
query:
WITH titled AS (
  SELECT 'Constraint test' AS label, id, title FROM constraint_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Invariant test' AS label, id, title FROM invariant_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Specification test' AS label, id, title FROM specification_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Policy test' AS label, id, title FROM policy_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Domain service test' AS label, id, title FROM domain_service_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Use case test' AS label, id, title FROM use_case_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'View test' AS label, id, title FROM view_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Endpoint test' AS label, id, title FROM endpoint_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Flow test' AS label, id, title FROM flow_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Integration test' AS label, id, title FROM integration_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Pattern rule test' AS label, id, title FROM pattern_rule_test
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Standard rule test' AS label, id, title FROM standard_rule_test
)
SELECT id AS record,
       label || ' ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which says what it tests or should do; title a test by the result it shows, such as "An overdue loan is refused a renewal".' AS message
FROM titled
WHERE regexp_matches(lower(trim(title)), '^(should|it should|tests? (that|whether|if))([^a-z]|$)')
ORDER BY record

name: title-breaks-convention
summary: A capability or use case title that breaks its naming convention: an interface named in it, a capability starting with The or an -ing word, or a list.
explanation: A capability is named as a noun phrase for a lasting ability of the business, two to four words: subject and activity noun, such as Invoice management or Member registration, or a single noun when the area is clear on its own, such as Catalog or Lending. A use case is named for one goal of its actor, verb first: verb and object, such as Borrow a tool or Approve an invoice, two to six words. Neither names a screen, a tool or a technology: a use case happens through interfaces, with one flow each, so the interface belongs to its flows, not its title. The check reads only the mechanical parts, in any letter case and as whole words: a use case or capability title that holds one of its product's interface titles or the words command line, CLI, desktop app, web app, MCP, API, agent tools, command layer or page (or their plurals); a capability title of two or more words that starts with "The" or with an -ing word (a word of five or more letters ending in -ing, other than the few that are not verbs, such as thing, string and evening), so a single noun such as Lending passes; and either title that holds a list, a comma followed later by "and" or "or". Two goals joined by "and" with no comma are not read, nor is a use case title that does not start with a verb. Rename the capability or use case by the convention.
query:
WITH titled AS (
  SELECT 'Use case' AS label, u.id, u.title, s.product_id FROM use_case u JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = u.id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Capability', c.id, c.title, s.product_id FROM capability c JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = c.id
),
words AS (
  SELECT label, id, title, product_id,
         ' ' || trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g')) || ' ' AS padded,
         split_part(trim(regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g')), ' ', 1) AS first_word
  FROM titled
),
found AS (
  SELECT label, id, title,
         coalesce(
           (SELECT min(n.name) FROM (
              SELECT trim(regexp_replace(lower(i.title), '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g')) AS name FROM interface i WHERE i.product_id = w.product_id
            ) n
            WHERE n.name <> '' AND contains(w.padded, ' ' || n.name || ' ')),
           nullif(regexp_extract(w.padded, ' (command lines?|clis?|desktop apps?|web apps?|mcp|apis?|agent tools?|command layers?|pages?) ', 1), '')
         ) AS interface_word,
         label = 'Capability' AND first_word = 'the' AS starts_the,
         CASE WHEN label = 'Capability' AND contains(trim(padded), ' ') AND length(first_word) >= 5 AND first_word LIKE '%ing'
                   AND NOT list_contains(string_split('thing string spring during evening morning ceiling nothing something everything anything', ' '), first_word)
              THEN first_word END AS starts_ing,
         contains(title, ',') AND regexp_matches(lower(substr(title, strpos(title, ','))), '[^a-z](and|or)([^a-z]|$)') AS lists
  FROM words w
)
SELECT id AS record,
       label || ' ' || id || ' is titled "' || trim(title) || '", which '
       || concat_ws('; it ',
            CASE WHEN interface_word IS NOT NULL THEN 'names an interface or mechanism ("' || interface_word || '")' END,
            CASE WHEN starts_the THEN 'starts with "The"' END,
            CASE WHEN starts_ing IS NOT NULL THEN 'starts with the -ing word "' || starts_ing || '"' END,
            CASE WHEN lists THEN 'holds a list (a comma, then "and" or "or")' END)
       || CASE WHEN label = 'Use case'
               THEN '; name a use case for one goal of its actor, verb first, such as "Borrow a tool", and leave the interface to its flows.'
               ELSE '; name a capability as a noun phrase for a lasting ability of the business, such as "Payment processing" or "Lending".' END AS message
FROM found
WHERE interface_word IS NOT NULL OR starts_the OR starts_ing IS NOT NULL OR lists
ORDER BY record

name: too-many-children
summary: A record with more children of one kind than its product's max_children setting.
explanation: The setting is the product's product_setting row (15 when it has none). A parent with that many children of one kind is missing a level between them, such as a capability or another aggregate. Children are counted per kind. Tests are exempt: they are read under what they prove. Children are also counted per group, read from the record_group view, since each group reads under its own heading: a flow's steps per path, since each path reads as its own list, and the records of every kind with a `group_name` (terms, UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and a product's own kinds) per `group_name`; the ungrouped ones are one list. Paths and groups are compared trimmed and in any letter case. Add a level, or a group, and move the children into it.
query:
WITH children AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.kind, p.parent_id, coalesce(g.label, '') AS label
  FROM record_parent p
  JOIN meta_kind k ON k.name = p.kind
  LEFT JOIN record_group g ON g.id = p.id
  WHERE p.parent_id IS NOT NULL AND k.stage IS DISTINCT FROM 'test-plan'
),
counted AS (
  SELECT parent_id, kind, lower(trim(label)) AS bucket, min(trim(label)) AS label, count(*) AS n
  FROM children GROUP BY parent_id, kind, lower(trim(label))
)
SELECT c.parent_id AS record,
       pk.label || ' ' || c.parent_id || ' has ' || c.n || ' children of kind ' || c.kind
       || CASE WHEN c.kind = 'flow_step' AND c.bucket <> 'main' THEN ' on path ' || c.label
               WHEN c.kind <> 'flow_step' AND c.bucket <> '' THEN ' in group ' || c.label ELSE '' END
       || ', more than the ' || coalesce(ps.max_children, 15)
       || ' that the product''s max_children setting allows; add a level between them, such as a capability or another aggregate.' AS message
FROM counted c
JOIN record_id p ON p.id = c.parent_id
JOIN meta_kind pk ON pk.name = p.kind
JOIN record_scope s ON s.id = c.parent_id
LEFT JOIN product_setting ps ON ps.product_id = s.product_id
WHERE c.n > coalesce(ps.max_children, 15)
ORDER BY record, message

name: ui-component-unused
summary: A ui component that nothing uses.
explanation: A ui component has no owner: it exists because it renders views. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the views it renders with renders, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'UI component ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: it renders views; link the views it renders with renders, or remove it.' AS message
FROM ui_component r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM renders x WHERE x.source_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: value-object-unused
summary: A value object that nothing uses.
explanation: A value object has no owner: it exists because fields of entities, value objects, events or read models are typed with it. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Type the fields that hold it with it, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'Value object ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: fields of entities, value objects, events or read models are typed with it; type the fields that hold it with it, or remove it.' AS message
FROM value_object r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entity_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM value_object_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM event_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM read_model_field f WHERE f.type_value_object_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record

name: view-route-not-in-file
summary: A view whose route no file of the UI components that render it names.
explanation: A view's route is the address it is shown at, and the UI components that render it show it there, so one of their files names the route, written any way routes are written (`/tools/{toolId}`, `/tools/:toolId`, `/tools/<tool-id>`, `/tools/[toolId]`, a template's `${toolId}`, or a regular expression literal that matches it, such as `/^\/tools\/(\d+)$/`), in code, a string or a comment. Parameters match whatever their names, and only the path counts: a query string or fragment is not part of a route. Then a reader of the record finds the code, and an address changed on one side and not the other is caught. A view with no route, or whose components' files do not exist yet, is not checked. Correct the view's route, or name it in the file of the component that shows the view at that address.
query:
SELECT r.record,
       'View ' || r.record || ' is at ' || r.route || ', but no file of the UI components that render it (' || r.files
       || ') names that route; correct the view''s route, or name it in the file of the component that shows the view there.' AS message
FROM route_facts r
WHERE r.kind = 'view' AND r.files <> '' AND NOT r.found
ORDER BY record

name: view-unused
summary: A view that nothing uses.
explanation: A view has no owner: it exists because flow steps happen in it. One that nothing uses is a leftover, or a link is missing. Link the steps that happen in it with happens_in, or remove it.
query:
SELECT r.id AS record, 'View ' || r.id || ' is used by nothing: flow steps happen in it; link the steps that happen in it with happens_in, or remove it.' AS message
FROM view r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM happens_in h WHERE h.target_id = r.id)
ORDER BY record
